A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MRI reconstruction work. All 13 pages of v2 and 14 pages of v3, including appendices, equations, tables, and figures, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original fastMRI knee and brain reconstruction experiments, super-resolution evaluations, and kernel-interpolation and parameter-matched analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds an ablation evaluating the frequency-space NOk module.

M1.justification: The NOk initialization, unrolled NOi/data-consistency updates, UDNO architecture, and SSIM objective are retained. Naming the kernel basis as Zernike polynomials adds specification; the PDFs do not establish a replacement of the implemented basis or another procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same fastMRI knee and brain coverage, undersampling patterns and rates, higher-resolution reconstruction, and extended FOV. The new ablation uses existing patterns; zero-shot evaluation across patterns was already present in v2, including Table 6.

E2.justification: The existing benchmark comparator sets are retained. Figure 12 adds a comparison against a model without NOk, introducing an ablated comparator without expanding the external baseline set.

E3.justification: The new NOk ablation trains both variants on a small subset of the 4x equispaced training data and evaluates zero-shot SSIM across patterns. Existing experimental protocols remain unchanged; the newly specified cascade count and baseline-search settings are additional disclosures.

E4.justification: Appendix D and Figure 12 add a targeted test of NOk's contribution to generalization across undersampling patterns. The existing kernel-interpolation and matched-parameter analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Existing plus/minus reporting and shaded variability bands are retained, and Figure 12 follows the existing plotting practice. No new seed information, repeated-run counts, confidence-interval definitions, or significance tests are reported.

E6.justification: Table 3 changes E2E-VN inference time from 0.25 s to 0.06 s, matching the unchanged NO time. Section 4.2 newly reports a 1.8 dB zero-shot PSNR advantage, and Appendix D reports a 5.3% SSIM benefit from NOk across irregular patterns. Reconstruction values in Tables 1, 2, and 5–7 are unchanged.

T1.justification: New Appendix E substantially expands formal coverage beyond v2's Euclidean convolution formulas and qualitative limit discussion. It adds group-convolution and DISCO definitions, a matrix formulation, an explicit CNN grid-refinement limit, and Zernike orthogonality and completeness reasoning in Equations 9–14.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about a unified resolution-agnostic MRI model, robustness across undersampling patterns, efficiency, super-resolution, and extended FOV.

C2.justification: v3 expands the architectural rationale around multiscale context and fine details, and contrasts MRI high-frequency information with typically smooth PDE data. Section 4.2 also distinguishes clinical settings with known versus unknown patterns. The existing DISCO-only and diagnostic-accuracy limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 specifies 12 cascades and names the Zernike basis. Appendix B.4 and Table 8 disclose CSGM Bayesian tuning on six non-test images for about 50 iterations, including parameter ranges and distributions, and identify tuned E2E-VN settings. Existing hardware, architecture details, and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds Born and Wolf's Principles of Optics for the Zernike discussion and expands the comparison with FNO's treatment of frequencies. The remaining cited works and central novelty positioning are retained after matching renumbered references.

P1.justification: Localized explanations are expanded in the method, experimental discussion, and Appendix A. The appendix roadmap and implementation heading are revised, and Sections B.4 and E are added. The main narrative and section organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds hyperparameter-search Table 8 and ablation Figure 12. Existing figures and tables undergo limited resizing, relocation, and surrounding text reflow, including Figures 9 and 11 and Table 3; their existing visual evidence is retained.

improvement.justification: The baseline-search disclosure improves reproducibility, Figure 12 supplies direct evidence about NOk's contribution, and Appendix E makes the mathematical rationale more self-contained. These are useful but limited gains: the new ablation's exact training subset and budget remain unspecified, and the new 1.8 dB result lacks a detailed accompanying breakdown.
